definitions.explanation: a dining arrangement where customers pay a fixed price to eat as much as they want within a time limit

examples.japanese: 2000{円|えん}で{焼肉|やきにく}{食|た}べ{放題|ほうだい}だ。
{食|た}べ{放題|ほうだい}のケーキバイキングに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to an all-you-can-eat cake buffet.

examples.japanese: {制限時間|せいげんじかん}は90{分|ふん}で{食|た}べ{放題|ほうだい}だ。
examples.english: It's all-you-can-eat with a 90-minute time limit.

notes:
FORMATION:
{食|た}べる (to eat) + {放題|ほうだい} (as much as one wants)

PATTERN:
The ～{放題|ほうだい} pattern is productive:
- {飲|の}み{放題|ほうだい} (all-you-can-drink)
- {歌|うた}い{放題|ほうだい} (all-you-can-sing/karaoke)
- {見|み}{放題|ほうだい} (watch all you want, e.g., streaming)
- {乗|の}り{放題|ほうだい} (unlimited rides)

TYPICAL FEATURES:
- Fixed price ({定額|ていがく})
- Time limit ({制限時間|せいげんじかん}) - usually 60-120 minutes
- May have extra charges for premium items
- Often penalty fees for leftover food

ALTERNATE TERMS:
- バイキング (Viking - used for buffets in Japan)
- ビュッフェ (buffet)

RELATED:
- {飲|の}み{放題|ほうだい} (all-you-can-drink)
- バイキング (buffet)
- {定額|ていがく} (fixed price)
